Definition: of Hebrew origin (H609); Asa, an Israelite:--Asa.
BiblicalUsage: Asa is named in the genealogy of Jesus, as the son of Abijah and the father of Jehoshaphat, in the line of kings that runs from David to the exile. The Greek text behind the King James reads Asa here, while the later Greek text reads Asaph, so the verse stands on the Textus Receptus reading.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Asa belongs in the line because he is the king who sought the LORD with all his heart and took away the idols, and his name in the genealogy is a reminder that the King who was promised comes through kings who, at their best, sought God.
